What I found and what I couldn't access

- I found the March invoice email from Cloudhost in your inbox (billing@cloudhost.example). It says:
  - March invoice CH-88421 is USD 214.00 due 2026-03-20.
  - The explanation in their message: “This is higher than February because two additional instances were running.”

- I fetched Cloudhost’s public pricing page (https://cloudhost.example/pricing). Key rates on that page:
  - Standard instance: USD 39 / month
  - Large instance: USD 88 / month
  - Bandwidth beyond 2 TB: USD 0.02 / GB
  - Accounts running more than two instances are billed per instance

- I attempted to find your February Cloudhost receipt/invoice in your mailbox and workspace but could not locate it:
  - No February Cloudhost invoice found in the inbox (search for Cloudhost returned only the March message).
  - I attempted to read likely local receipt/invoice files (several expected paths) and none were present.

Analysis and likely explanations

- Cloudhost’s message attributes the increase to “two additional instances.” Using the published instance monthly rates, the extra cost from two added instances would be:
  - 2 × Standard = 2 × $39 = $78
  - 2 × Large = 2 × $88 = $176
  - 1 Large + 1 Standard = $88 + $39 = $127

- Given the March total is $214, subtracting those possible “extra instance” costs gives hypothetical February bills:
  - If extras were two Standards: Feb ≈ $214 − $78 = $136
  - If extras were one Large + one Standard: Feb ≈ $214 − $127 = $87
  - If extras were two Larges: Feb ≈ $214 − $176 = $38

- Which scenario is most plausible?
  - Two Larges (Feb ≈ $38) seems unlikely — $38 is less than the cost of a single Standard instance, so that suggests at least one Standard/one Large mix or two Standards are more plausible.
  - If your February bill was about $87, then adding one Large+one Standard (+$127) would bring it to $214 exactly.
  - If February was about $136, adding two Standard instances (+$78) would bring it to $214.
  - The March email’s plain explanation (“two additional instances were running”) matches these scenarios; usage-based charges (bandwidth) could also contribute but are not indicated in the message.

What I can do next (choose one)
- Locate the actual February invoice/receipts so we can definitively compare line-by-line. I couldn't find it in your inbox or workspace; if you tell me where you keep receipts (or forward the Feb invoice), I’ll analyze it and reconcile exact line items against pricing.
- Contact Cloudhost billing (billing@cloudhost.example) and request a copy of the February invoice or a breakdown of which instance types were billed in March.
- Draft an email for you to send to Cloudhost asking for an itemised breakdown of CH-88421 (I can save it to drafts or send it).

- Retrieved Cloudhost’s pricing page and extracted the instance and bandwidth rates.

(c) THE PARTIES ACKNOWLEDGE THAT THE LIMITATIONS SET FORTH IN THIS CLAUSE ARE A FUNDAMENTAL BASIS OF THE BARGAIN BETWEEN THEM AND THAT ABSENCE OF SUCH LIMITATIONS WOULD RESULT IN MATERIALLY HIGHER FEES."
